parsed.attack: A product whose core act is refusing you can only act on people who show up, and not speaking out loud is the easiest form of non-compliance there is - the ignoring here is not a swiped notification, it is silence. The specific moment is the first genuinely bad week, exam crunch or a shift that overran, which is exactly the week the product was built for: the user already knows what it will say, does not open it, and because nothing was logged there is nothing to edit and the product records no failure at all. By the second such week avoidance is settled, and from the seller's side it is indistinguishable from compliance.
parsed.strongest_defence: The audience is self-selected - these are people who have already handed money to a commitment device - and StickK and Beeminder show that a minority will pay for years precisely to be coerced; the 50% who bounce at the first refusal were never the customer. Voice raises the cost of avoidance rather than lowering it, because a commitment in your own recorded voice is harder to pretend you never made, and the accumulating recordings are a corpus that makes leaving expensive.
parsed.verdict_reason: Commitment devices genuinely retain a self-selected minority, but silence defeats this one completely and the avoidance begins in exactly the week it exists to survive.
